items.title: Public Hearing Matters under the Planning Act (advertised)
notes: This is a formal public meeting to consider applications under the Planning Act. In accordance with the Ontario Planning Act, only the applicant or owner of land affected by the planning applications, a specified person, or a public body, and or the Minister may appeal most decisions.  If you do not make a verbal submission to the Committee or Council, or make a written submission prior to City Council making a decision on the proposal, you may not be entitled to appeal the decision of the City of Kitchener to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT), and may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT. To understand your right of appeal, if any, or for further clarification regarding appeals, please see the Ontario Land Tribunal website.

items.title: Kitchener 2051 – New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235
notes:
Councillor P. Singh declared a conflict on this item. (Councillor P. Singh declared a conflict regarding the Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, related to the Strategic Growth Area Designations in the Highland Road-Belmont Street, Connaught Street-Franklin Street South and the Stirling Street-Mill Street vicinities, due to their family members owning property, and did not participate in any discussion or voting on this matter.)

The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-235, dated May 21, 2026, recommending approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/002/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/003/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/014/COK/JZ; and approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/015/COK/JZ. It was noted written submissions were received by the following: H. Jaeger, L. Johnson, T. Nagy , A. Ostapchuk, A. Sinclair, B. Brockelbank, C. Cardoso Cote, C. Palmer, C. Parsons, D. Aston, the Downtown Action Advisory Committee, G. Billo, H. Kendall, H. Mackay, I. Jagas, J. Spence, K. Barber, L. Garvey, M. Stauch, V. Hicks, M. Baya, S. Feick, S. Tiessen, C. Tsimenidis, J. Seally, A. Gilani, S. Mavor, T. O'Donnell, M. Reid and D. Reid, K. Doehn, D. Beamer, B. Trotter, J. Alati, N. Jenson, Region of Waterloo, Zehr Group, M. Bradshaw, H. Knapp and D. Kuehl.

R. Bustamante, Director, Planning and Housing Policy, provided opening remarks. J. Zunic, Senior Planner and R. Noye, provided an overview of the report. N. Goss, Manager, Policy and Research, and G. Stevenson, Director, Development and Housing Approvals were also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic entered the meeting at this time.

B. Trotter addressed the Committee, noting concern that without explicit policy protections, cultural heritage landscapes such as the Westmount neighborhood, remain at risk due to incremental intensification.

P. Chauvin, MHBC Planning, representing Activa Holdings Inc. and 1000682913 Ontario Inc., addressed the Committee, noting concerns with the proposed parkland dedication policies, specifically highlighting that trails are no longer included in parkland dedication calculations.

A. Milne addressed the Committee, noting concerns regarding the potential negative impacts of policies 3.7 to 3.10, as well as the lack of application of institutional zoning to existing institutional lands in the downtown area.

S. Nevin addressed the Committee, identifying two areas of concern, specifically the proposed six-storey height permissions within Neighbourhood Growth Areas and the implications for the Westmount West area.

M. Stauch and T. O’Donnell addressed the Committee, noting concerns regarding proposed increases in permitted building heights in the Auditorium neighbourhood, citing potential impacts on infrastructure, traffic and pedestrian safety, and Cultural Heritage Areas.

G. Shepherd and J. Kossowski addressed the Committee regarding concerns related to the level of intensification proposed for the Westmount neighbourhood, however indicated support for Option 2.2.1(a) as outlined in the staff report.

D. Aston, MHBC Planning, addressed the Committee regarding concerns with proposed Official Plan designations for 526 Lancaster Street West, Hesh Crescent and Shirley Avenue, 809 Wellington Street, and lands at Brigadoon-Strasburg Road and Robert Ferrie Drive, requesting amendments to extend the “Commercial First” designation, retain employment flexibility through Staff Option 2.1(a), reinstate a Special Policy Area to recognize existing uses, and designate the lands at Strasburg Road and Robert Ferrie Drive as Strategic Growth Area and Mixed Use B.

H. Price, GSP Group, and G. O’Brien, Davies Howe, on behalf of Schlegel Urban Developments, addressed the Committee and identified concerns with several Official Plan policies, specifically: 4.12, 11.42–11.48, 11.9, 11.51–11.53, 11.SPA.35, and 12.58–12.61 and 12.103. Specific concerns were cited related to potential constraints on permitted uses, reduced flexibility, and added uncertainty in development approvals and application requirements.

S. Martinello addressed the Committee regarding land use designations in the Auditorium neighbourhood, noting inconsistencies with Strategic Growth Area criteria and requesting that lands outside Major Transit Station Areas be designated as Neighbourhood Growth Area with a Neighbourhoods land use designation and a three-storey height limit.

K. Muir, Zehr Group, addressed the Committee, noting concerns with the proposed redesignation of 1373 and 1381 Victoria Street North from “Commercial” to “Auto-Oriented Commercial;” citing a reduction in permitted uses and potential impacts on long-term leasing flexibility and property viability.

H. Jaegar addressed the Committee, noting concerns with Policy 3.10 and the application of Institutional designations, citing potential impacts on achieving a balanced housing mix, supporting complete communities, and ensuring appropriate recognition and protection of existing institutional lands.

items.title: Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, Cont'd
notes:
The Committee continued consideration of Development Services Department report DSD-2026-235, dated May 21, 2026, recommending approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/002/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/003/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/014/COK/JZ; and approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/015/COK/JZ.

M. Bowman, Waterloo Region Yes in My Backyard, noted support for the Kitchener 2051 New Official Plan, highlighting its approach to increasing housing supply, enabling intensification, and promoting growth across all neighbourhoods.

D. Galbraith, UP Consulting, on behalf of 585 Bridgeport Road East and 514 Lancaster Street West, addressed the Committee and requested that the properties be designated as a “Strategic Growth Area” in Map 2 – City Structure and “Mixed Use B” in Map 3 – Land Use in place of the designations proposed by City Staff.

C. Stockie, Kitchener Downtown Advisory Committee, addressed the Committee, noting concerns with Policy 6.70(a), due to the potential for ward-based tree canopy targets to mask neighbourhood-level inequities, and recommended establishing canopy targets at the neighbourhood level to better support equitable distribution.

A. Sinclair, MHBC Planning, on behalf of multiple properties, addressed the Committee and identified concerns including the need to recognize and permit continued and expanded office uses at 520 Bingemans Centre Drive, reinstate site-specific permissions for 425 Bingemans Centre Drive, support Staff Option 2.1(a) for 525 Bingemans Centre Drive and 355 Shirley Drive, and designate the Huron/Strasburg lands as a Strategic Growth Area in recognition of planned intensification and existing approvals.

P. Nickels addressed the Committee and requested that the Institutional land use designation be applied to all qualifying properties, including those within Protected Major Transit Station Areas.

E. Elliot, MHBC Planning, on behalf of 6 Shirley Avenue, addressed the Committee, requesting support for Staff Option 2.1(a), as well as the retention of a “Commercial First” designation and existing Special Policy Area permissions for 6 Shirley Avenue to maintain established commercial and office uses.

C. Patel and R. Khunkhun addressed the Committee on behalf of 239–265 Mill Street and requested a change from Mixed Use A to Mixed Use B to better support the site’s development potential.

A. Vantyghem, Strong Towns Waterloo Region, addressed the Committee in support of the proposed Official Plan, emphasizing intensification, diverse housing, and the importance of not allowing heritage preservation to limit growth.

In response to questions from the Committee regarding the Westmount West Cultural Heritage Landscape (CHL), N. Goss noted that staff priority over the next year is to initiate an Archaeological Master Plan, as the current plan has not been updated since 1989. N. Goss further advised that, given recent legislative changes, existing staff resources, and budget constraints, the City does not have capacity at this time to undertake additional Cultural Heritage Landscape studies, and therefore no timeline has been established for a Westmount CHL.

In response to questions from the Committee regarding trails and parkland dedication, N. Goss noted that parkland dedication is intended for programmable park spaces, and that the acquisition of trails would be addressed on a case-by-case basis. Staff further advised that trail corridors forming part of the park may qualify, whereas those functioning solely as active transportation corridors would not, and would instead need to be secured through subdivision negotiations. It was noted additional clarity will be provided to Council at the June 29, 2026 Council Meeting.

In response to questions from the Committee regarding institutional lands, N. Goss noted that land use designations were not changed through this Official Plan process.

items.title: Kitchener 2051 - New Official Plan, DSD-2026-235, Cont'd
notes:
The Committee continued consideration of Development Services Department report DSD-2026-235, dated May 21, 2026, recommending approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/002/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/003/COK/JZ; approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/014/COK/JZ; and approval of City Initiated Official Plan Amendment OPA26/015/COK/JZ. 

A motion was brought forward by Councillor S. Davey to approve the staff recommendation as outlined in Development Services Department Report, DSD‑2026‑235.

Due to the declared conflict of interest by Councillor P. Singh, it was noted that the Strategic Growth Area designations in the Highland Road–Belmont Street, Connaught Street–Franklin Street South, and Stirling Street–Mill Street vicinities would be considered and voted on separately.

The following amendments to the main motion were then introduced:

Councillor M. Johnston brought forward an amendment that the Westmount neighbourhood be incorporated into the New Official Plan with the city structure, land use, and cultural heritage landscape policies as outlined in Option 2.2.1.a.

Councillor M/ Johnston's amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor S. Stretch brought forward an amendment that the Auditorium neighbourhood be incorporated into the New Official Plan with the city structure, land use, and cultural heritage landscape policies as outlined in Option 2.2.2.a, with the exception that lands currently designated Medium Rise Residential in the 2014 Official Plan be designated Mixed‑use A, as recommended.

Councillor S. Stretch's amendment was then voted on and was Carried. 

Councillor S. Davey brought forward the following amendment:

That the portion of 526 Lancaster Street West currently designated “Business Park Employment” in the City’s 2014 Official Plan be designated “Commercial First” on Map 3 Land Use and that a new site specific provision be added to this portion of the property not permitting residential uses; and,

That 809 Wellington Street North be removed as an “Industrial Growth Area” and identified as a “Neighbourhood Growth Area” on Map 2 City Structure and that a site specific policy be added as follows:

Notwithstanding the General Industrial land use designation on the lands legally known as part of Lots 32,33, and 34, Registered Plan 763, more particularly described as Parts 1 to 3 on Reference Plan 58R-3130 and Part 1 on Reference Plan 58R-10424, municipally known as 809 Wellington Street North, the following uses will also be permitted:

i. Offices, not including major offices, up to 100% of the gross floor area;

ii. Research and development;

iii. Facilities that are ancillary to the permitted uses in the General Industrial designation;

iv. Construction uses and contractor/service trades;

v. Printing and publishing operations;

vi. Repair operations;

vii. Catering uses;

viii. Automotive service stations, and automotive repair and detailing;

ix. Complimentary service uses such as restaurants, print shops, computer service facilities, financial establishments, personal services, fitness centres, recreational facilities, day care facilities, health offices and clinics and veterinary services provided:

i. They are located within a building containing at least one primary permitted use as identified in policy 11.105;

ii. No individual unit used will exceed 1,500 square metres of gross floor area; and,

iii. They will not conflict or interfere with the satisfactory operation and development of the lands for General Industrial purposes.

That 6 Shirley Avenue be removed as an “Industrial Growth Area” and identified as a “Neighbourhood Growth Area” on Map 2 City Structure and designated “Commercial First” on Map 3 Land Use and that a new site specific provision be added to permit Major Office and to not permit residential uses, and;

That 355 Shirley Avenue and 525-555 Bingeman Center Drive be removed as an “Industrial Growth Area” and identified as a “Neighbourhood Growth Area” on Map 2 City Structure and that a site specific policy be added as follows:

a) Notwithstanding the General Industrial land use designation on the lands municipally known as 355 Shirley Avenue and 525-555 Bingeman Center Drive, the following uses will also be permitted:

i. Agriculture;

ii. Campground;

iii. Commercial recreation entertainment uses;

iv. Conference, convention or exhibition facilities

v. Convenience retail;

vi. Hotels and motels

vii. Offices, not including major offices, up to 100% of the gross floor area;

viii. Research and development

ix. Construction uses and contractor/service trades;

x. Printing and publishing operations;

xi. Repair operations;

xii. Catering uses;

xiii. Automotive service stations, and automotive repair and detailing;

xiv. Complimentary service uses such as restaurants, print shops, computer service facilities, financial establishments, personal services, fitness centres, recreational facilities, day care facilities, health offices and clinics and veterinary services provided:

i. They will not conflict or interfere with the satisfactory operation and development of the lands for General Industrial purposes.

5. That the lands legally described as Part of Blocks 4, 5 and 6 on Plan 58m-424, being Parts 2-9, 12-19 on 58R-16128- be removed as an “Industrial Growth Area” and identified as a “Neighbourhood Growth Area” on Map 2 City Structure and that a site specific policy be added as follows:

a) Notwithstanding the General Industrial land use designation on the lands legally described as Part of Blocks 4, 5 an6 on Plan 58m-424, being Parts 2-9, 12-19 on 58R-16128, the following uses will also be permitted:

i. Offices, not including major offices provided it is located within 450 metres of an existing or planned transit corridor;

ii. Research and development;

iii. Construction uses and contractor/service trades;

iv. Printing and publishing operations;

v. Repair operations;

vi. Catering uses;

vii. Automotive service stations, and automotive repair and detailing;

viii. Complimentary service uses such as restaurants, print shops, computer service facilities, financial establishments, personal services, fitness centres, recreational facilities, day care facilities, health offices and clinics and veterinary services provided:

i. They are located within a building containing at least one primary permitted use as identified in policy 11.105;

ii. No individual unit used will exceed 1,500 square metres of gross floor area; and,

iii. They will not conflict or interfere with the satisfactory operation and development of the lands for General Industrial purposes.

Councillor S. Davey's amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor S. Davey brought forward a further amendment that 1373 and 1381 Victoria Street North be designated “Commercial First” on Map 3 (Land Use).

Councillor S. Davey's further amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor B. Ioannidis brought forward an amendment that 239–265 Mill Street be designated “Mixed‑use B”.

Councillor B. Ioannidis' amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor P. Singh brought forward an amendment that the lands south of Ottawa Street South, between Fischer‑Hallman Road and Kingswood Drive, and north of the hydro corridor, be redesignated from “Strategic Growth Area” on Map 2 and “Mixed‑use A” on Map 3 to “Neighbourhood Growth Area” on Map 2 and “Neighbourhoods” on Map 3.

Councillor P. Singh's amendment was then voted on and was Carried. 

The staff recommendation outlined in Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-235, excluding the portions subject to Councillor P. Singh’s declared conflict of interest, was then voted on and Carried.

The remaining portions of the staff recommendation relating to the Strategic Growth Area designations in the Highland Road–Belmont Street, Connaught Street–Franklin Street South, and Stirling Street–Mill Street vicinities were subsequently voted on, and were Carried.
